transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… things at home have been getting to me more than usual. My father-in-law moved in with us, and I’m still managing okay at work, but when I’m home, or trying to keep up with coursework, I’m more tense and short with people than I’d like.

I’ve also stopped doing some of the things that usually help me clear my head—fishing, woodworking, those first-aid workshops. So… I figured I should come in before it gets worse.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying the things you used to, like fishing or woodworking, or have you just been too busy or stressed to do them?

A bit of both, I guess. I’m not sure I’d say I don’t enjoy them anymore… it’s more that since my father-in-law moved in, I’m wound up at home and with coursework, and I just don’t make it out fishing or get into the woodworking. Same with the first-aid workshops. Those usually help clear my head, but I’ve been skipping them.
Would you say that, even if you had the time and space, you wouldn’t enjoy those activities as much as you used to, or do you think you’d still enjoy them if you could just make the time?

I think I’d still enjoy them if I could get myself to make the time. It’s not that fishing or woodworking feels pointless now… I’ve just been more wound up since my father-in-law moved in, and by the time I’m home or dealing with coursework, I end up skipping the things that usually clear my head.
Have you noticed that activities like fishing or woodworking feel less enjoyable or rewarding to you now, even when you do manage to do them?

Not really less rewarding, no. When I actually do them, I think they still help. It’s more that I’ve been wound up since my father-in-law moved in, and I end up skipping them instead of making the time.
Do you find yourself worrying about things even when there isn’t a specific problem or stressor, or does your worry tend to go away once the situation is resolved?

It’s mostly tied to what’s going on, I think. Since my father-in-law moved in, I’ve just been more wound up at home, and it spills into my coursework. I’m holding it together at work, but when that stress is there, I get short and stop doing the things that usually keep me level.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried even about things unrelated to your father-in-law or coursework, like everyday situations or small decisions?

Not so much unrelated things. It really started after my father-in-law moved in. I’m keeping it together at work, but at home and with coursework I’m more wound up and short than usual… and I’ve been skipping the stuff that usually clears my head, like fishing or woodworking.
Have you noticed any anxiety or tension that sticks around even when things are calm at home and you’re not dealing with coursework?

Not really when things are calm, no. It’s more since my father-in-law moved in… I can keep it together at work, but at home and with coursework I get more wound up and short. And then I stop doing the things that usually help, like fishing or woodworking.
Have you noticed that, even when you do get a chance to go fishing or do woodworking, you don’t get the same sense of satisfaction or enjoyment out of it as you used to?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really gone much lately, so it’s hard to say. When I do, I think it still helps some… I just haven’t been making the time for it.
Have you felt like you don’t care about things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities altogether—even the ones you used to enjoy like fishing or woodworking?

I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest altogether. It’s more like… since my father-in-law moved in, I’m just more wound up at home and with coursework, and I end up skipping fishing, woodworking, even the first-aid workshops—stuff that usually clears my head. I still care about them, I just haven’t been doing them.
Have you felt like you don’t enjoy or care about things as much as you used to, even when you’re not stressed about home or coursework?
I haven’t really noticed that, no. If things are actually calm, I think I still care about those things. It’s just… I haven’t had much of that calm lately.
Have you ever felt like you’ve completely lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like fishing or woodworking—even when things weren’t stressful at home or with coursework?
No, I don’t think completely. I mean, I haven’t had much space where things weren’t stressful, but I don’t feel like those things are gone for me.
Have you ever had a period where you didn’t care about things you usually enjoy—like fishing or woodworking—even when things weren’t stressful at home or with coursework?
Not really, no. I can’t think of a time when things were calm and I just didn’t care about any of it. It’s more that I haven’t had much room for it lately.
Have you noticed any time in the past when you didn’t take pleasure in things like fishing or woodworking, even when things at home or with coursework weren’t stressful?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had less time for those things, but I can’t point to a calm period where I just didn’t enjoy them.

Have you ever had a time when you didn’t feel like doing any of the things you usually enjoy—like fishing or woodworking—for no clear reason, even when things at home and with coursework were going smoothly?
No… I can’t really say that’s happened for no reason. If I’m not doing those things, there’s usually something going on or I’m just tied up.

Have you ever had a time when you didn’t feel like doing any of the things you usually enjoy—like fishing or woodworking—for no clear reason, even when things at home and with coursework were going smoothly?
I don’t think so. Like I said, if I pull back from that stuff, there’s usually some reason behind it. Not just out of nowhere.
